title: 3 dead after 2 helicopters collide midair near Oregon airport, sheriff says | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Investigators were combing through debris scattered across a field in northwest Oregon Fridayafter two helicopters collided midair, killing three people and forcing the closure of a nearby highway, officials said.

Oregon pilot Tyler Sturdevant, 38, died in the crash, along with Texas flight instructor Maddie Aasbo, 22, and 31-year-old student pilot Christopher Joughin from the United Kingdom, Yamhill County Sheriff Sam Elliott said during a news conference. Aasbo and Joughin were in one helicopter and Sturdevant was the sole occupant of the other, the sheriff said.

The aircraft crashed to the ground in a private farm field near McMinnville Municipal Airport, officials said, with a red helicopter left crumpled in pieces and a green helicopter lying upside down. McMinnville is about 40 miles southwest of Portland.

A one-mile stretch of nearby Highway 233 remained closed Friday due to the crash, according to theOregon Department of Transportation, giving no estimate for reopening.

Leo Rodriguez said he called 911 after witnessing the crash from his family vineyard.

“All of a sudden I hear this big boom and this metal breaking, and I look up and just see these two helicopters just collided in mid-air,” he toldCNN affiliate KPTV.

“It took me a while for my brain to figure out what I was seeing. You don’t see this every day. They twisted and fell to the ground.”

The sheriff’s office asked the public to avoid the area and have “patience as we respond to this critical incident.”

The investigation into the crash, which took place around 2:10 p.m. local time, is being led by the National Transportation Safety Board with help from the FAA and the helicopter airframe and engine manufacturers, the federal agency said during a Friday news conference.

NTSB investigators arrived at the scene Friday morning and were in the process of documenting the crash site.

“We expect to be completed with the on-scene and recovery later this evening,” NTSB investigator Grant Mills said Friday. “Tomorrow, we will be conducting interviews with witnesses and the operators of the aircraft.”

The two aircraft involved were a Robinson R-22, which was the instructional flight, and an Airbus AS350, which was on a maintenance flight, the NTSB said.

Investigators were working Friday to retrieve equipment containing flight instrument data from the Airbus AS350, Mills said. The agency was still determining whether the Robinson R-22 had similar equipment.

One of the helicopterswas operated by Jerry Trimble Helicopters, a helicopter flight training school and rental service for private flights, the company said in astatement.

“Jerry Trimble Helicopters is deeply saddened to confirm that one of our aircraft was involved in an aviation incident this afternoon,” the company said. “Our hearts and thoughts are with the individuals involved, their families, and everyone affected by this event.”

The company added it is cooperating with authorities in the investigation.

This story has been updated with additional information.
